exercise1.prompt: Array Maths and Broadcasting: Centre on the mean

hiddenCases.name: one value is its own mean
the subtraction reaches the whole array at once

exercise1.hint: values - values.mean() does the whole thing. np.round then rounds the array, and tolist() turns it back into plain numbers.

exercise2.prompt: Array Maths and Broadcasting: Apply a weight to every column

hiddenCases.name: uneven weights favour the right column
broadcasting applies the weights
hiddenCases.describe: the weights broadcast across the rows

exercise2.hint: (table * weights) scales every row by the weights, because the shapes line up on the right. Then sum along axis=1 for one total per row.

choices: The 5 is broadcast to the array’s shape
questions.explain: The scalar is treated as though repeated to fit, without a real array of fives ever being built.

questions.prompt: Which pair of shapes cannot broadcast?
questions.explain: Lined up from the right, dimensions must be equal or one of them must be 1. 3 and 4 are neither.

questions.prompt: What does values - values.mean() give you?
choices: Each value’s distance from the average
questions.explain: Centring a column, and the first half of standardising it.

questions.prompt: table has shape (2, 3). Which array can be added to it row-wise?
questions.explain: Shapes line up from the right, so the (3,) matches the 3 columns and is applied to every row.
